work.name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
work.summary: As an academic researcher on the front line of discovery about the way the Earth works, I coded data analysis algorithms on a daily basis (mostly Matlab), delivered dozens of presentations, and collaborated on numerous research projects with colleagues from around the world. Check out the publications tab of my website for additional details.
highlights: Produced the first high-resolution seismic image of continental lithosphere subducting into the mantle beneath Northern Greece, a controversial result (see Pearce JGR 2012 paper)

Developed novel approaches for using seismic images to quantitatively assess the validity of tectonic/geodynamic models, e.g. measuring ~70 km of differential slab rollback induced offset across the Cephalonia Transform Fault in Western Greece, consistent with geologic and geodynamic modeling estimates

Identified a reflector interpreted as the base of the external Hellenides thin-skinned thrust belt and discovered that it breaches the surface where basement rocks are exposed within the footwall of active extensional faults, as predicted by geodynamic modeling, compelling evidence for how continental crust forms in retreating subduction settings

Developed a preprocessing pipeline to generate receiver functions from array data with unprecedented fidelity and accuracy, while expanding the number of earthquakes available for imaging (i.e. it made lower signal-to-noise EQs viable for imaging)
Derived analytical expressions for receiver function imaging of 3D, dipping interfaces with multiple layers to power a Common Conversion Point imaging algorithm
Managed and quality controlled over a dozen big (TB+) data sets, 6+ for publication

Developed 12+ data processing workflows combining signal processing (FFT, PCA, adaptive filtering) and machine learning (linear regression, genetic algorithms) — early applications of quantitative ML methods to geophysical inverse problems
Trained research teams to apply seismic imaging workflows on their own datasets, resulting in several peer-reviewed publications

Developed an automated multichannel alignment pipeline (Appendix B of PhD thesis) replacing a manual qualitative process with an iterative, convergence-based automated system — a direct precursor to modern MLOps thinking

Presented over twenty times at conferences and universities, including invited talks for the Tectonics Observatory Brownbag Seminar at Caltech in July of 2011 and the Department Seminar at the University of Oregon in January of 2011
Tech: MATLAB, Python, Signal Processing (FFT, PCA, Filtering), Linear Regression, Genetic Algorithms, Distributed Computing, Seismic Imaging

projects.name: AgentFluent
projects.summary: Local-first Python CLI on PyPI that analyzes Claude Code and Claude Agent SDK session traces to diagnose agent configuration quality and recommend improvements.
highlights: Created deterministic evaluation pipelines that correlate prompt design, tool selection, model configuration, retry behavior, token usage, and execution errors with actionable optimization recommendations

Scores every recommendation on one of three diagnostic axes — cost (token spend, model selection trade-offs), speed, and quality (mid-flight user corrections, file rework density, reviewer-caught rate) — exposing per-recommendation axis_scores and primary_axis in the JSON envelope so a CI rule can gate on a single dimension
Enhanced quality diagnostics with opt-in git and GitHub enrichment layers that correlate session behavior to downstream CI failure rates, PR review density, and feat-to-fix commit proximity
Implemented rolling baseline regression detection, structured JSON outputs, CI/CD integration, automated versioning, and quality gates using GitHub Actions, mypy, pytest, ruff, and release-please

Designed a privacy-first, zero-cost architecture that runs locally with no outbound network calls unless GitHub enrichment is explicitly opted into, enabling enterprise-safe agent evaluation, monitoring, and continuous improvement

Extracted the supervised dev-loop engine powering AgentFluent's own development into a standalone Claude Code marketplace plugin, making the same structured, human-gated development loop available to any project
Tech: Python, Pydantic, PyYAML, pytest, mypy, ruff, GitHub Actions, Loop Engineering

Implemented personalized coaching that generates optimized prompts, identifies missing collaboration behaviors, and correlates fluency scores with token consumption, cache utilization, and development cost

Architected cross-platform Python and TypeScript services with persistent caching, structured JSON parsing, GitHub CLI integration, and comprehensive automated testing exceeding 1,650 unit and integration tests

Built a production-ready analytics platform that turns raw Claude Code conversations into actionable engineering insights through interactive visualizations, research-backed scoring models, and repository-specific recommendations

projects.name: Sportswear ESG News Classifier
projects.summary: Fully autonomous production ML pipeline monitoring ESG news for 50+ global sportswear brands, publishing a live Sustainability Scorecard and interactive dashboard.
highlights: Architected and deployed an autonomous production ML pipeline that monitors ESG news for 50+ global sportswear brands, classifies articles through a hybrid ML and LLM workflow, and publishes a live Sustainability Scorecard with evidence-backed rankings, sentiment analysis, and searchable dashboards

Built a two-stage classification pipeline using Random Forest (F2: 0.974) and Logistic Regression (F2: 0.931) pre-filters ahead of Claude-based ESG classification, reducing inference costs by 20-30% while preserving high recall for relevant content

Created a RAG pipeline with OpenAI embeddings, PostgreSQL, and pgvector to retrieve supporting article passages for every ESG classification, providing traceable evidence instead of opaque model outputs

Automated end-to-end operations with Python orchestration for news collection, drift detection, model evaluation, website publishing, and health reporting, replacing 5-10 hours of weekly manual effort at an operating cost of about $0.15/day

Deployed and maintained production infrastructure using FastAPI, Docker, Google Cloud Run, MLflow model registry, Evidently AI, GitHub Actions CI/CD, and a 900+ test suite supporting continuous delivery and monitored model performance
Tech: Python, Claude API, OpenAI Embeddings, scikit-learn, Jupyter, FastAPI, Docker, Google Cloud Run, PostgreSQL, pgvector, MLflow, Evidently AI, GitHub Actions

projects.name: E-Commerce Fraud Detection
projects.summary: Production-grade fraud detection REST API combining feature engineering, model training, explainability, automated testing, and cloud-native deployment (ML Zoomcamp capstone).
highlights: Built a production-grade fraud detection service combining feature engineering, model training, explainability, automated testing, and cloud-native REST APIs to evaluate real-time payment transactions with configurable business risk thresholds

Developed an XGBoost classifier achieving 0.87 PR-AUC with 73% precision at 83% recall on a 299K transaction dataset with a 44:1 class imbalance, transforming 15 raw fields into 30 domain-specific behavioral and transaction features

Implemented five configurable decision threshold strategies and TreeSHAP-based prediction explanations, enabling fraud teams to balance false positives against fraud losses while providing transparent, analyst-ready decision rationale

Designed and deployed a FastAPI service with Pydantic validation, multi-stage Docker containers, and Google Cloud Run auto-scaling, sustaining 25 requests/second at under 70ms server-side P99 latency under Locust load testing
Validated production reliability through a 448 test suite covering preprocessing, feature engineering, model inference, explainability, API endpoints, and integration workflows
Tech: Python, XGBoost, scikit-learn, Jupyter, FastAPI, Docker, Google Cloud Run, SHAP, Pydantic, Pytest, Locust

projects.name: US Presidential Election Analysis
projects.summary: Multi-source ETL pipeline and public REST API serving U.S. Electoral College and popular vote data from 1824 to present, live at api.us-presidential-election-center.org.
highlights: Built a multi-source ETL pipeline ingesting U.S. Electoral College and popular vote data from the National Archives (web scraping), MIT Election Lab (CC0 dataset), and UCSB American Presidency Project, reconciling sources onto shared candidate and state keys in a PostgreSQL star schema warehouse spanning elections from 1824 to present

Designed a read-only SQLite snapshot architecture that fully decouples the API serve path from the live database — the Docker container serves requests with Postgres stopped, eliminating runtime database dependencies and enabling scale-to-zero Cloud Run deployments within the free tier

Deployed a public FastAPI REST API (api.us-presidential-election-center.org) fronted by Cloudflare for CDN caching, rate limiting, and bot protection; implemented keyless CI/CD via Workload Identity Federation GitHub Actions with version-based cache invalidation on cutover

Implemented rigorous data licensing compliance: MIT Election Lab data served under CC0 1.0, non-redistributable UCSB data excluded from the public API, with provenance metadata embedded in every response envelope

Publishes the 'Counted, Not Assumed' blog series documenting two centuries of presidential election data from primary sources, supported by an automated cross-repo publishing pipeline with fail-closed OG card validation and validate-all-then-write atomicity guarantees
Tech: Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Docker, Google Cloud Run, Cloudflare, GitHub Actions, BeautifulSoup, pandas, geopandas, uv
